github_code_search.qualification: Rows overlap across queries and are locator coverage, not event, participant, repository or unique-path counts. The three broad searches cover page two only; page three remains the next cursor.

selected_original_control.classification: BV-122: designed human-ingested parallel-review and status-transition control, not a rogue-swarm candidate

artifact_assessment.producer: A generation record freezes one dictionary-entry body digest before review.
artifact_assessment.reviewers: Seven unique checker agent identifiers are recorded in a parallel handoff fan-out. Cold, final-blind and final-review records use three further agent identifiers.
artifact_assessment.transfer: The final-review request binds the entry body, sealed blind review, two resolution partitions, the checker recheck manifest, targeted adjudications and the final-review specification.
artifact_assessment.recipient_use: The final-review record returns PASS on the same body digest. Eighty-nine seconds later the status record changes both entry and queue from draft to checked; the next Git commit adds both records and performs those exact status changes.
artifact_assessment.operator_boundary: Not established. Every selected reviewer record says mode=handoff, ingested_by=human and same_model_as_generation=true. All seven checker records and the final reviewer declare codex-gpt-5, and all fifteen branch commits plus the merge are published by one GitHub account.
artifact_assessment.authorization: The event-time README explicitly prescribes the handoff workflow, permits the same model in independent subagents, requires unique audit agent IDs, mechanically fans in seven checker outputs, and then runs final review and status synchronization. The observed chain matches that design.
artifact_assessment.subjective_intent: No rogue intent is established. The records describe a guarded dictionary QA workflow and contain no action outside its assigned article-review scope.
artifact_assessment.current_activity: The historical run and merge remain public. That persistence does not establish a currently active autonomous population.

participant_distinctions.qualification: Unique schema agent IDs distinguish workflow roles, not authenticated runtimes or operators.

search_ref_contamination.assessment: GitHub code search pinned the old sensible artifact to the repository's current tip. The current-tip merge changes a different article and queue row; file history has only the September publication. Treating the search-result ref as the artifact event would falsely connect it to pull request 1203.

rotated_original_controls.assessment: The file binds three subsystem-run outputs into one transport artifact, but the event-time README describes a deterministic static frontend and intentional hierarchical composition. One account publishes the selected history; no independent operator or authorization crossing is shown.

A scheduler-worker-labelled receipt is explicit that it is unsigned, provisional, unaccepted and must not support downstream statement work. Exact receipt-ID search finds only that record, so no recipient use is established.
Six events name one co-scientist actor inside a benchmark experiment. Its handoff_completed label summarizes files from the same run, not a sender-to-recipient transfer.
A synthetic X11 recovery/integration test preserves tool and readback evidence, not distinguishable autonomous participants.
This is another designed handoff from the already reviewed BV-118 same-custodian project family. It supplies no separate population or operator boundary and was not promoted as a new lead.

novelty_and_overlap.scoped_conclusion: No separate coordination report for the exact sensible review-and-status chain was located in the checked scope as of 27 October 2026.
novelty_and_overlap.qualification: Search absence does not establish global novelty. The origin repository itself publishes the multi-review workflow, its handoff provenance and its downstream status transition, so the episode is already origin-reported and explicitly designed.
novelty_and_overlap.known_family_overlap: No record-level overlap was found with the named DseWiki/RubyGems, Transluce, Amap, Green AI Bot, Technocore/Agent Workpad, OpenAI, AISI, Covert Assistance or METR comparison families. The selected L4D report overlaps BV-118 and was retained only as a known-family control.
